name: Machha Besara
instructions: 1. Marinate the fish pieces with salt and turmeric, then shallow fry in mustard oil until golden brown and set aside.
2. Prepare a fine paste by grinding soaked mustard seeds, garlic cloves, and dried red chilies with a little water.
3. In the same pan, sauté potato wedges until light brown.
4. Add the mustard-garlic paste to the pan, along with turmeric, salt, and tomato chunks; cook until the oil separates.
5. Pour in sufficient water to create a thin gravy and bring to a boil.
6. Gently slide the fried fish into the gravy and simmer for 5-7 minutes.
7. Garnish with fresh coriander leaves and serve hot with steamed rice.
description: Machha Besara is a quintessential Odia delicacy that showcases the region's love for mustard-based gravies. It is a staple in many households, often served during lunch, and reflects the coastal influence where fresh river fish and mustard are key culinary components.
